Ancient Indian history

Indian history timeline: from prehistory to 1947

Indian history runs from stone tools over a million years old, through the Harappan cities of about 2600 to 1900 BCE, the Vedic and Mahajanapada periods, the Maurya and Gupta empires, regional kingdoms, the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals, to British rule and independence on 15 August 1947.

We run museum gallery studies and period walks that turn this timeline into objects and monuments, for schools, colleges and adult groups.

How Indian history is divided into periods

Historians usually split the Indian past into prehistory (no writing), protohistory (writing exists but cannot be read, as with the Harappan script), and the historical period, which in India starts in earnest with the inscriptions of Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Textbooks then use the broad labels ancient, medieval and modern. These are conveniences, not hard walls: the early medieval period from about 600 to 1200 CE is now treated as a phase in its own right.

Dates before the Mauryas are approximate. Many come from radiocarbon results on excavated material and from the relative order of pottery and soil layers, explained in our guide to how archaeologists date artifacts. Where a date below says about, treat it as a range of a century or more.

Ancient India: from the first cities to the Guptas

The first Indian cities belong to the Indus Valley Civilization, whose mature phase lasted roughly seven centuries. You can stand on one of its largest sites at Rakhigarhi in Haryana, a short drive from Delhi. After the cities declined, the Vedic period is known mainly through texts, and the archaeology of the Ganga plain picks up again with Painted Grey Ware settlements.

From about the 6th century BCE the Mahajanapadas competed for power, and Magadha won. The Mauryan empire became the first state to rule most of the subcontinent, and Ashoka's edicts are India's earliest deciphered writing. The Gupta empire of the 4th to 6th centuries CE is remembered for its coins, sculpture and the first stone temples.

Early medieval and medieval India

After the Guptas, power was regional. Kanauj in the Ganga plain was contested by the Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan, a three-way rivalry textbooks call the tripartite struggle. In the south the Chola dynasty built a maritime state and the great temple at Thanjavur.

The Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 and ended at the first battle of Panipat in 1526, when Babur founded the Mughal empire. In the Deccan, the Vijayanagara empire and the Bahmani sultanate and its successors dominated from the 14th to the 16th century. Delhi itself was rebuilt several times in this period, which is why people speak of the seven cities of Delhi.

Modern India: Company, Crown and independence

Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) in 1498 and the English East India Company was chartered in 1600. The Company became a territorial power after Plassey in 1757 and Buxar in 1764. The Revolt of 1857 ended Company rule, and from 1858 India was governed directly by the British Crown.

The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Gandhi returned from South Africa in 1915 and led the non-cooperation movement from 1920, the Salt March in 1930 and the Quit India movement in 1942. India became independent on 15 August 1947, the same moment the subcontinent was partitioned.

Seeing the timeline on the ground

A timeline is easier to remember when each row has a place attached to it. Delhi alone holds an Ashokan rock edict, an Ashokan pillar moved by Firoz Shah Tughlaq, Sultanate tombs, Mughal forts and the 1857 sites of Kashmere Gate. Our Delhi through seven cities day threads several of these together, and a museum morning with an archaeologist at the National Museum covers the Harappan, Mauryan and Gupta galleries in a single visit.

Questions people ask

What are the main periods of Indian history?

Indian history is usually divided into prehistory (the Stone Age), protohistory (the Harappan and Chalcolithic cultures), the ancient period (Vedic age to the Guptas and their successors), the medieval period (Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara, Mughals) and the modern period (European companies, British rule and the national movement up to 1947).

When did ancient Indian history begin?

There is no single start date. Human presence in India goes back over a million years through stone tools. The first cities appear with the Harappans around 2600 BCE. The historical period, with readable written records, begins with Ashoka's inscriptions in the 3rd century BCE.

Which was the first empire in India?

The Maurya empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 321 BCE, is generally regarded as the first empire to control most of the Indian subcontinent. Magadha under the Nandas was already a large kingdom before it, but the Mauryas extended rule from Afghanistan to Karnataka.

When did medieval Indian history start?

Many textbooks start the medieval period with the Delhi Sultanate in 1206. Historians increasingly treat about 600 to 1200 CE as an early medieval phase, marked by regional kingdoms, land grants and temple building, so medieval India is often counted from around the 7th century.

How should I memorise the Indian history timeline?

Learn a few anchor dates first: 2600 BCE for Harappan cities, 321 BCE for the Mauryas, 320 CE for the Guptas, 1206 for the Sultanate, 1526 for the Mughals, 1757 for Plassey, 1857 and 1947. Then hang each dynasty on those anchors and link each to a monument you can picture.
